subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should this TUI issue be solved first as a renderer/dependency scrollback fix, as a local TUI viewport/autofollow feature, or as an explicit user setting?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the durable fix depends on whether maintainers want to patch or upgrade pi-tui, add local anchoring behavior, or expose a new user-facing TUI policy surface.

options.title: Renderer-first fix
options.body: Pursue a pi-tui patch, dependency upgrade, or narrow dependency override that preserves scrollback and viewport stability before adding new user-facing settings.

options.title: TUI autofollow feature
options.body: Define and implement TUI-specific follow-lock or jump-to-latest behavior if maintainers want a product-level viewport model independent of pi-tui internals.

options.title: Wait for upstream
options.body: Keep this open while waiting for a maintained upstream pi-tui fix, accepting that current TUI users still have the disruptive behavior meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Renderer-first fix
recommendation.body: Pursue a pi-tui patch, dependency upgrade, or narrow dependency override that preserves scrollback and viewport stability before adding new user-facing settings.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses pi-tui dependency ownership and TUI product semantics, and steipete has the strongest recent history across dependency and TUI-shape work.
